note: Hand-picked starting points. Sizes are approximate download sizes for the default quantization. RAM is a rough working-set figure — running several at once needs the sum, which is why the local lane defaults to 2.

models.name: qwen2.5:3b
models.use: Fast general-purpose worker. A good first pull and a solid default for sub-agents.

models.name: llama3.2:3b
models.use: Strong instruction-following at a small size. Good summarizer and extractor.

models.name: llama3.2:1b
models.use: Smallest useful model here. For simple classification and formatting on modest hardware.

models.name: qwen2.5:7b
models.use: Noticeably better reasoning than the 3B tier. A reasonable local big agent.

models.name: qwen2.5-coder:7b
models.use: Code-specialised. Pair it with the Coder agent.

models.name: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b
models.use: Small code model for quick edits and explanations.

models.name: mistral:7b
models.use: Well-rounded general model with a direct writing style.

models.name: gemma2:2b
models.use: Very fast, good at short focused tasks. Weak on long reasoning.

models.name: gemma2:9b
models.use: Capable mid-size generalist for machines with headroom.

models.name: phi3.5:3.8b
models.use: Punches above its size on reasoning. Good critic on small hardware.

models.name: deepseek-r1:7b
models.use: Reasoning-focused. Slower per answer — best for planning, not fan-out workers.

models.name: deepseek-r1:1.5b
models.use: Tiny reasoning model. Useful when RAM is tight.

models.name: llama3.1:8b
models.use: Dependable all-rounder with good long-context behaviour.

models.name: nomic-embed-text
models.use: Embeddings only — not a chat model. Listed so you know what it is if you see it.
